title: Polk County School Board, District 3 (runoff)
what_it_does: School board members set the district budget and school millage, hire and evaluate the superintendent, approve curriculum materials, and set district policy.

school_books.summary: Wallace says she is a firm believer in parental rights and in transparency about a child's own access, but that one family's preferences should not automatically decide for every other family; she frames her role as applying state law and the district's review process.

candidates.name: Victor Sims
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.background: Sims, 30, is a senior program officer whose career has been in child and family advocacy and social work. He is a former foster youth from Polk County who says he attended 12 schools, and he is the parent of a child with an individualized education plan. He holds degrees from Polk State College, the University of South Florida, Florida International University and Florida State University's law school, and finished second in the August 2026 District 3 primary.

taxes.summary: Supports the district's 1-mill property-tax referendum on the Nov. 3 ballot, which would raise money mostly for employee pay.

teacher_pay.summary: Sims made "Backing Our Teachers & School Staff" one of three campaign messages, calling for better pay, stronger retention efforts and working conditions that keep teachers in the profession, and said the same applies to bus drivers, cafeteria workers and aides. His campaign website calls for competitive salaries for staff.
teacher_pay.quote: We need to respect that with real investment—better pay, stronger retention efforts, and working conditions that allow teachers to actually stay in the profession they love.

sources.title: Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey - Victor Sims

school_safety.summary: Sims said student mental health resources, along with IEP and ESE services, should be consistently reachable across the district, and he tied school success to support systems for children inside and outside the classroom. His website lists school safety as a responsibility but he framed his approach around student supports rather than policing or discipline.
school_safety.quote: That means strengthening academic support, expanding opportunities in arts and career pathways, and making sure services like IEPs, ESE support, and student mental health resources are actually reachable and consistent across the district.

sources.title: Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey - Victor Sims

school_books.summary: Says a parent may keep their own child from a challenged book, but other parents should be able to choose to opt in; one family's objection should not decide for all.
school_books.quote: If a parent doesn't want their child reading a challenged book, I respect that. But another parent should have the ability to review it and choose to opt in. One family's choice shouldn't have to become every family's choice.
